precepts.text: False brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage: the bondage of the sacrifice system again. Our liberty is that Christ died on the cross; we are free from that burden.
precepts.point: I marvel that ye are so soon removed unto another gospel: which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ. The same men from Acts 15. Though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed. The gospel they pushed was going back to sacrificing; that is another gospel.

note.label: Traitors and Their Exquisite Subtlety: The Judas Iscariot Effect

precepts.why:
“I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another”. It is not another because it is found in the law of Moses. “but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.” They are the same men of Acts 15, who went out from us and troubled the churches. Paul says, if any man preach any other gospel, “let him be accursed”. Those men were running around joining the churches and causing confusion by infiltration, pushing a gospel we are no longer under: going back to sacrificing animals. That is another gospel.

Chapter 2 names them: “And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage”. The liberty we have is that we no longer offer up animals. Christ died on the cross, and we are free from that burden. The bondage they wanted to bring us into was sacrificing animals again to be saved, like Acts 15.

So Galatians 5 says “Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.” If animal sacrifice saves you, Christ died for nothing and you are fallen from grace. Yet “ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh”: do not use this freedom to do what you want and sin.

Likewise today, Christians will come in here and do the same thing: accept the identity, but not the theology, using the same book and the same Bible to push Christianity. That is the same infiltration in reverse. As John says, “They went out from us, but they were not of us”, and those who trouble you shall bear their judgment.

precepts.text: Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently. Peter came back and taught it after he learned: we cannot have fake love for the brethren, because God already showed me; and when I was put to the test, I was influenced not to accept them. So now the message is: do not have feigned love for the brethren.
precepts.point: If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews? Peter knew better. He was corrected in front of them all, and he would have been embarrassed and ashamed. But he repented; and as a teacher, what do you teach after that? What you repented from: do not be fake.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
James, Cephas and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, “that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.” The heathen are the northern kingdom. Peter already knew this. God had shown him that he could not call any man common or unclean. He sat with them, and he convinced many of the Jews that these men were all right, that God had granted them repentance unto life too.

“But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.” When certain came from James, Peter “withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.” Dissimulation means deception, hypocrisy, pretence, deceit, fakery: in other words, being fake. Paul said to him before them all, you are being fake like they were fake. Peter knew better, and he was corrected in front of everybody. He would have been embarrassed and ashamed.

But he repented. And as a teacher, what do you teach after that? What you repented from: do not be fake. So Peter wrote “Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently”.

Peter came back and taught it after he learned it: I was wrong. We cannot have fake love for the brethren, because God already showed me, and when I was put to the test I was influenced not to accept them. So the message now is, do not have feigned love for the brethren.

precepts.text: Then said the Jews, whither will he go that we shall not find him? Will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles? The dispersed are Israelites, and the Jews of the circumcision call the dispersed Israelites Gentiles. Now you know who the Gentiles are that Paul writes to.
precepts.point: Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ. Here is where the other gospel and the error of the wicked come in: all you have to do is believe, you can lie, cheat, steal, and rape in the name of Jesus, as a Dominican in the Bronx once told me. Works of the law, law singular, shout out to Captain Zakar: the law of sacrifice from Nehemiah 10:33. A man no longer receives atonement by sacrificial law, for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. Christians will run to Galatians 2:16, 3:2, and 3:5; these are their go-tos, and I am giving you the tools.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
Paul keeps saying “among”: the gospel “which I preach among the Gentiles”, preaching him “among the heathen”. Why does he keep using that word? Because Israel was scattered among the nations, and that is who he is writing to the entire time. Then he says “the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter”. Christ wrought effectually in Peter toward the Jews born and raised in the law and circumcised the eighth day, “the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles”.

Who are those Gentiles? John answers: “Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” The Jews here are the circumcision, born and raised in the Mosaic law. They ask where Christ will go that they cannot find him. Will he go to the dispersed? The dispersed are the Israelites, the diaspora scattered among the Gentiles.

And what do the Jews call those dispersed Israelites? Gentiles: “and teach the Gentiles”. So now you know who the Gentiles are that Paul writes to throughout the entire time. It should be a no-brainer now.

That is why James, Cephas and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, “that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision”: Paul to the Israelites scattered among the nations, the others to the Jews who were not scattered abroad. And it is why Paul withstood Peter at Antioch. Peter ate with these Gentiles, the scattered Israelites he was teaching who they are, then withdrew when certain came from James, fearing them of the circumcision. You cannot teach the scattered who they are and then act as if you are not with them; that is a bad example.

precepts.point: There were always checks and balances. The leadership would steer you in the right direction.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Paul's second visit to Jerusalem, fourteen years after his first, is the history of Acts 15, and the majority of Paul's epistles and the issues he addresses extend around that chapter. “And certain men which came down from Judea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” That meant getting circumcised to reestablish the covenant with Abraham and giving an animal sacrifice to reestablish the covenant of Moses.

“When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.” He went up by revelation, the spirit of the Lord leading him to Jerusalem. On the way “they passed through Phenice and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles”, and when they came to Jerusalem “they were received of the church, and of the apostles and elders, and they declared all things that God had done with them.”

“privately to them which were of reputation” refers to the apostles and elders. “lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain” means Paul had to check with the leadership to confirm he was on the right path. There were always checks and balances; the leadership would steer you in the right direction.

precepts.point: There were always checks and balances. The leadership would steer you in the right direction.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem” counts from the first trip: “Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days.”

So the first visit was three years after his conversion on the road to Damascus, and this second visit was fourteen years after that. This time he went up by revelation, with Barnabas and Titus, and laid the gospel he preached among the Gentiles before those of reputation.

precepts.point: Paul warns in 1 Corinthians 9:27 that he keeps his body under subjection lest he himself become a castaway.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The “false brethren unawares brought in” are identified in Acts 15: “But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.”

These were believers, of the sect of the Pharisees, who infiltrated the congregation with this doctrine. “was compelled to be circumcised” shows the Pharisees were going around forcefully telling people they had to be circumcised and return to animal sacrifice. Titus, being a Greek, brought up in Greek customs and fashion like Timothy whose father was a Greek, was an Israelite raised in Greek ways, not a Caucasian, and these false brethren wanted him circumcised to bring him into bondage.

precepts.point: Paul warns in 1 Corinthians 9:27 that he keeps his body under subjection lest he himself become a castaway.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Titus was one of those drawn away by this false doctrine. He eventually forsook Paul: “For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.”

The same Titus who stood with Paul in Jerusalem and was not compelled to be circumcised later fell away through these doctrines about circumcision and animal sacrifice. If Titus could fall, anybody could fall.

precepts.point: Paul warns in 1 Corinthians 9:27 that he keeps his body under subjection lest he himself become a castaway.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Titus was an elder of the highest rank. Paul wrote “To Titus, mine own son after the common faith”, and charged him, “For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee.”

A man Paul called his own son, who ordained elders in every city, who had a book written after him, yet fell away through the doctrines of circumcision and animal sacrifice. That is how strong the false brethren's bondage was, and if Titus could fall, anybody could fall.

precepts.point: Paul warns in 1 Corinthians 9:27 that he keeps his body under subjection lest he himself become a castaway.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Paul himself did not take his standing for granted: “But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.”

If Titus, an elder of the highest rank, could be drawn away by the false brethren, then even the one who preached to others could become a castaway. Paul kept his body under subjection because of it.

precepts.point: Only through Christ could all 12 tribes receive salvation.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
After the dispute about circumcision and animal sacrifice, Peter switches to the topic of the Gentiles: “Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe. And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us; And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.”

The reason he switches is this: if salvation required circumcision and animal sacrifice, the old covenant, then the northern kingdom, called Gentiles, strangers, heathens, could never receive salvation. So Peter asks, “Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?” That yoke is the bondage the false brethren were trying to bring the brethren into.

precepts.point: Only through Christ could all 12 tribes receive salvation.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The northern kingdom were strangers from the covenants: “at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world.” If salvation stood in circumcision and animal sacrifice, they could never have it.

“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us; Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace; And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross.”

That is the liberty we have in Christ Jesus that the false brethren came in privily to spy out. The wall between the two kingdoms is broken down by the blood of Christ, not by circumcision and sacrifice.

precepts.point: Only through Christ could all 12 tribes receive salvation.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
How the northern kingdom became strangers from the covenants: Jeroboam “said in his heart, Now shall the kingdom return to the house of David: If this people go up to do sacrifice in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again unto their lord, even unto Rehoboam king of Judah, and they shall kill me.” So he “made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. And he set the one in Beth–el, and the other put he in Dan.”

The northern kingdom was excommunicated because Jeroboam prohibited them from going to Jerusalem to sacrifice. Cut off from the sacrifice, they could never be saved under a covenant that required animal sacrifice, which is why the false brethren's doctrine would have shut them out.

precepts.point: Only through Christ could all 12 tribes receive salvation.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Tobit lived through the northern kingdom's cutting off. “all the tribe of Nephthali my father fell from the house of Jerusalem, which was chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, that all the tribes should sacrifice there, where the temple of the habitation of the most High was consecrated and built for all ages. Now all the tribes which together revolted, and the house of my father Nephthali, sacrificed unto the heifer Baal.”

“But I alone went often to Jerusalem at the feasts, as it was ordained unto all the people of Israel by an everlasting decree”, bringing the firstfruits and tenths to the priests the children of Aaron. Tobit alone kept going up; the tribes that revolted were away from the sacrifice at Jerusalem. That is the northern kingdom, strangers from the covenants, who could never be saved if salvation required animal sacrifice.

precepts.point: Only through Christ could all 12 tribes receive salvation.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The woman of Samaria shows the same divide: “Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.” Christ answered, “Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.”

The northern tribes had been kept from Jerusalem, the place of sacrifice, and worshipped in their own mountain. The hour was coming when worship would be neither there nor at Jerusalem, because salvation was coming by Christ and not by the sacrifice the false brethren wanted to bind on the brethren.

precepts.point: Only through Christ could all 12 tribes receive salvation.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The law fixed the sacrifice to one place: “unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there, even unto his habitation shall ye seek, and thither thou shalt come: And thither ye shall bring your burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, and your tithes, and heave offerings of your hand, and your vows, and your freewill offerings, and the firstlings of your herds and of your flocks.”

That place was Jerusalem. When Jeroboam forbade the northern kingdom to go up there, they were cut off from the only place the sacrifices could be brought. Under the old covenant of circumcision and animal sacrifice they had no way to be saved; that is why the doctrine of the false brethren could not stand.

precepts.point: That is why Christ is called the end of the law (of sacrifice) to them that believe. Ephesians 2:14-16 shows Christ broke down the middle wall of partition between the two kingdoms, abolishing in his flesh the enmity (the law of commandments contained in ordinances, meaning the sacrificial laws), making of twain one new man.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Christ hath “obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises. For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.”

The new covenant is made “with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah”, both kingdoms, “Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant.” The false brethren wanted to bring the brethren back into the first covenant of circumcision and sacrifice; the liberty in Christ Jesus is the better covenant, which takes in the northern kingdom that the first could never save.

precepts.point: That is why Christ is called the end of the law (of sacrifice) to them that believe. Ephesians 2:14-16 shows Christ broke down the middle wall of partition between the two kingdoms, abolishing in his flesh the enmity (the law of commandments contained in ordinances, meaning the sacrificial laws), making of twain one new man.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.”

The gifts and sacrifices were carnal ordinances imposed only until the time of reformation. To compel Titus to be circumcised and return to animal sacrifice was to go back to what could not make a man perfect, and to shut out the northern kingdom that had no access to it. That is the bondage the false brethren came in privily to bring.

precepts.point: That is why Christ is called the end of the law (of sacrifice) to them that believe. Ephesians 2:14-16 shows Christ broke down the middle wall of partition between the two kingdoms, abolishing in his flesh the enmity (the law of commandments contained in ordinances, meaning the sacrificial laws), making of twain one new man.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us; Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace; And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby.”

Both, the circumcision and the strangers from the covenants of promise, are made one in Christ. The ordinances of sacrifice that the false brethren wanted to reimpose were abolished in his flesh. That is why neither Titus nor anyone else was compelled to be circumcised: our liberty in Christ Jesus is the one new man made by the cross.

precepts.point: That is why Christ is called the end of the law (of sacrifice) to them that believe. Ephesians 2:14-16 shows Christ broke down the middle wall of partition between the two kingdoms, abolishing in his flesh the enmity (the law of commandments contained in ordinances, meaning the sacrificial laws), making of twain one new man.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“Take thy number, O Sion, and shut up those of thine that are clothed in white, which have fulfilled the law of the Lord.”

The ones counted to Sion are those clothed in white who have fulfilled the law of the Lord, not those who were compelled to circumcision and animal sacrifice by the false brethren. The liberty we have in Christ Jesus is what makes room for all of Sion's number, including the northern kingdom that the old covenant of sacrifice had shut out.

precepts.point: Eventually, if you are not of the elect, it will be manifest in your spirit and you will leave. The same thing happened in the apostles' time is happening today under different names but the same spirits.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The liberty in Christ Jesus is grace and mercy, and the false brethren were able to subvert believers from the gospel and persuade them outside of what they learned. John says the same: “Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists; whereby we know that it is the last time.” Antichrist is anybody against the mission or doctrine of Christ.

“They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us: but they went out, that they might be made manifest that they were not all of us.” They went out from the disciples, from the congregations and churches. Many of the deceivers and heretics come from the body itself, from those who are bitter and hold grudges.

You cannot fake this truth forever. Eventually, if you are not of the elect, it will be manifest in your spirit and you will leave. The same thing that happened in the apostles' time is happening today under different names but the same spirits.

precepts.point: Eventually, if you are not of the elect, it will be manifest in your spirit and you will leave. The same thing happened in the apostles' time is happening today under different names but the same spirits.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.”

The false brethren who went out from among the disciples were made manifest that they were not of us. Paul, who preached to others, kept his body under subjection so that he would not be a castaway. You cannot fake this truth forever; the one who does not keep himself under will be made manifest and leave.

precepts.point: This is how the truth of the gospel continues with the people.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The disciples did not give place to the heretics, “no, not for an hour.” As soon as they heard the heresy, they said you have to go. They did not give time for heretics to spread their doctrine because they understood there are weak-minded people in the body that are easily deceived. They did not debate heretics or argue with them.

Paul reads Psalms 51 every day, praying to endure and not become a castaway: “Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.” “Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me. Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.” That prayer is the guard against falling as the heretics fell.

Any heretical doctrine brought into the congregation is dealt with immediately. You come with any type of doctrines into the congregation, you will be removed. This is how the truth of the gospel continues with the people.

precepts.point: The circumcision was the southern kingdom of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi. The uncircumcised were primarily the northern kingdom.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The gospel of the uncircumcision was committed to Paul as the gospel of the circumcision was to Peter, both wrought by Christ. The uncircumcision was also called the Gentiles; these terms mean one and the same. “And the apostles and brethren that were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.” That refers specifically to Cornelius.

“And when Peter was come up to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him, Saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.” The circumcision contended with Peter for going to men uncircumcised: the two groups, circumcision and uncircumcision, are the two ministries of Galatians 2.

precepts.point: The circumcision was the southern kingdom of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi. The uncircumcised were primarily the northern kingdom.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Peter explains his encounter with Cornelius. The angel told Cornelius, “thy prayer is heard, and thine alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God”, and to send for Simon Peter. Peter said, “Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.”

Then verse 36 clarifies who is meant: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)”. The word was sent to the children of Israel. This cuts any doubt about Cornelius being of another nation: he was of the children of Israel in another nation, one of the uncircumcision, the Gentiles, that Paul's ministry was toward.

precepts.point: The circumcision was the southern kingdom of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi. The uncircumcised were primarily the northern kingdom.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit is there of circumcision?” The Jews were called the circumcision because they kept the covenant of circumcision established to Abraham.

The circumcision was the southern kingdom of Judah, Benjamin and Levi. The uncircumcised were primarily the northern kingdom. That is why Peter's apostleship was “of the circumcision” and Paul's was toward the Gentiles, the uncircumcision.

precepts.point: The circumcision was the southern kingdom of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi. The uncircumcised were primarily the northern kingdom.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.”

The twelve tribes were scattered abroad throughout all nations, starting from the Assyrian captivity onward. So when Peter says “in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him”, the word sent to the children of Israel finds them in every nation. Cornelius was one of the scattered, and the Gentiles of Paul's ministry are the tribes scattered abroad.

precepts.point: The circumcision was the southern kingdom of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi. The uncircumcised were primarily the northern kingdom.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.”

The two kingdoms are the circumcision, the southern kingdom of Judah, Benjamin and Levi, and the uncircumcised, primarily the northern kingdom. Peter's ministry to the one and Paul's to the other are both wrought by the same Christ, and they shall be no more two nations.

precepts.point: The circumcision was the southern kingdom of Judah, Benjamin, and Levi. The uncircumcised were primarily the northern kingdom.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Peter told Cornelius' house, “Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation; but God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.”

That is why the circumcision contended with Peter for going in to men uncircumcised. But the word God sent was unto the children of Israel, scattered into every nation; God showed Peter not to call these men common or unclean, and the gospel of the uncircumcision went to them by Paul.

precepts.point: This is why the northern kingdom Israelites in Acts 11:3 are called uncircumcised: they were not allowed to circumcise during the Greek captivity.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
How Israelites came to be uncircumcised: “king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people, And every one should leave his laws.” One people under one government and one religion, Hellenization. “Yea, many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed unto idols, and profaned the sabbath.”

The king sent letters to Jerusalem and the cities of Juda “that they should follow the strange laws of the land”, to forbid the offerings in the temple, to profane the sabbaths and festival days, to pollute the sanctuary and holy people, to set up altars and idols and sacrifice swine's flesh. And verse 48 specifically: “That they should also leave their children uncircumcised, and make their souls abominable with all manner of uncleanness and profanation.”

Many Israelites consented and left their children uncircumcised. That is the uncircumcision, the Gentiles, that the gospel was committed to Paul for.

precepts.point: This is why the northern kingdom Israelites in Acts 11:3 are called uncircumcised: they were not allowed to circumcise during the Greek captivity.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.”

Under Antiochus an Israelite could not keep the sabbath, keep the ancient feasts, or even profess himself to be a Jew. This is how Israelites became the uncircumcision: the laws of their fathers were outlawed, and their children were left uncircumcised.

precepts.point: This is why the northern kingdom Israelites in Acts 11:3 are called uncircumcised: they were not allowed to circumcise during the Greek captivity.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“For there were two women brought, who had circumcised their children; whom when they had openly led round about the city, the babes handing at their breasts, they cast them down headlong from the wall.”

Israelite women were killed for circumcising their children, led around the city and cast down headlong from the wall with their babies. Israelites who stopped circumcising under that terror became the uncircumcision. That is the people the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed to Paul for, just as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter.

precepts.point: They are called brethren of the Gentiles. Romans 9:3-4 proves the apostles' brethren are Israelites.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Verse 9 introduces a third term: the heathen. Paul was sent to the heathen, the same people called uncircumcision and Gentiles. Ezekiel shows who they are. God rebukes Israel for idolatry: “when ye make your sons to pass through the fire, ye pollute yourselves with all your idols, even unto this day: and shall I be enquired of by you, O house of Israel? As I live, saith the Lord God, I will not be enquired of by you.”

Then: “And that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all, that ye say, We will be as the heathen, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone.” Israel declared “We will be as the heathen” by following other nations' customs. When Israelites go outside their laws and follow other nations, they are called heathens.

precepts.point: They are called brethren of the Gentiles. Romans 9:3-4 proves the apostles' brethren are Israelites.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Even other nations recognized when Israel became like the heathen: “Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen.”

Moab and Seir looked at the house of Judah and said it was like all the heathen. That is the heathen Paul, Barnabas and the pillars agreed he should go unto: Israelites living as the nations around them.

precepts.point: They are called brethren of the Gentiles. Romans 9:3-4 proves the apostles' brethren are Israelites.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Ezra calls Israel heathen outright. “I Esdras received a charge of the Lord upon the mount Oreb, that I should go unto Israel; but when I came unto them, they set me at nought, and despised the commandment of the Lord. And therefore I say unto you, O ye heathen, that hear and understand, look for your Shepherd, he shall give you everlasting rest; for he is nigh at hand, that shall come in the end of the world.”

He was sent to Israel, and because they set the commandments of God at naught he calls them “ye heathen.” The Shepherd they are told to look for is Christ. So “that we should go unto the heathen” is Paul going to Israelites who had set the commandments at naught.

precepts.point: They are called brethren of the Gentiles. Romans 9:3-4 proves the apostles' brethren are Israelites.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The apostles' own letters confirm it. “Then pleased it the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; namely, Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren: And they wrote letters by them after this manner; The apostles and elders and brethren send greeting unto the brethren which are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia.”

They are called brethren of the Gentiles. The heathen, the Gentiles and the uncircumcision that Paul went to are the brethren.

precepts.point: They are called brethren of the Gentiles. Romans 9:3-4 proves the apostles' brethren are Israelites.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Who the apostles' brethren are: “I say the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Ghost, That I have great heaviness and continual sorrow in my heart. For I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh: Who are Israelites.”

The brethren are Israelites. So the “brethren which are of the Gentiles” in Antioch, Syria and Cilicia, the heathen Paul and Barnabas went to, are Israelites too.

precepts.point: They are called brethren of the Gentiles. Romans 9:3-4 proves the apostles' brethren are Israelites.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
When Paul came to Jerusalem the apostles perceived the Most High was dealing with him based on his ministry and the people he was waking up. You can tell the spirit on someone by how they move. Peter writes to those same people: “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.”

If the spirit of the Most High is in you, it compels you to keep pushing forward in the truth no matter how tired or exhausted, a lively stone built into the spiritual house. Those who are faking it can only do it for so long before they pull back, become less visible, and eventually leave.

precepts.point: They were given a charge to go to the brethren of the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The encounter Paul is explaining to the Galatians is recorded in Acts 15. “Then pleased it the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; namely, Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren.”

They were given a charge, with letters, “unto the brethren which are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia.” That is the fellowship Paul describes: the pillars sending him and Barnabas out with chief men of their own company, and Paul forward to do what they asked.

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
This is a very famous scripture used by Christians to argue against keeping the law, but Paul is making reference to a specific law. Romans settles that we are justified by keeping the commandments: “For not the hearers of the law are just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.”

The doers of the law shall be justified. So “the works of the law” by which no flesh is justified cannot be the commandments; it is a different law.

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
The law whose doers are justified is the commandments, as Romans 2 goes on to show. “Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God”, confident of being “a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness.” Then: “thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal? Thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?”

Do not steal, do not commit adultery, abhor idols: those are the commandments, and the doers of that law shall be justified. So we ARE justified by keeping the commandments, and the works of the law in Galatians 2:16 refer to a different law.

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Acts clarifies which law Paul means: “Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.”

Under the law of Moses, animal sacrifice, you could not be justified for certain sins like homosexuality, adultery, witchcraft: you were put to death. Through Christ is preached forgiveness of sins, and all that believe are justified from all things. That is the faith of Jesus Christ by which we are justified, and not by the works of that law.

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.” That proves why by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified: the sacrificial law never could take away sins.

“Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure. Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” The sacrifices and offerings “which are offered by the law” were temporary. When Christ came, sacrifice and offerings were no longer in effect, because Christ would be the ultimate sacrifice. We were not justified by the sacrificial law, but by Christ.

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” It was prophesied that the seed of Israel would be justified in the Lord, not by the blood of bulls and goats.

That is Galatians 2:16: “even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ.” The seed of Israel is justified in the Lord.

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith.”

The justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice. That is what Paul means by being “justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law.”

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“I will now remember the works of the Lord, and declare the things that I have seen: In the words of the Lord are his works.”

The works of the Lord are his words: his law, statutes and commandments. That is why the works of the law that justify no flesh cannot be the commandments themselves, whose doers are justified; they are the works of the sacrificial law of Moses that could not take away sins.

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt teach them ordinances and laws, and shalt shew them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do.”

The work they must do is the ordinances and the laws. Works, in scripture, are the keeping of what the Lord commands. The works of the law by which no flesh is justified are the works of the sacrificial law; the way wherein we must walk, the commandments, is still the work we must do.

precepts.point: Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“If a man be found lying with a woman married to an husband, then they shall both of them die, both the man that lay with the woman, and the woman: so shalt thou put away evil from Israel.”

Under the law of Moses there was no justification for adultery: both died. That is the law from which you could not be justified, and from which all that believe are justified through Christ. It is the works of that law that justify no flesh, not the commandments.

precepts.point: Proverbs 24:16 also applies: a just man falls seven times and rises up again.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Even while seeking to be justified by Christ, we are still found sinners, because “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.”

Even under Christ, if you break the law, you are a sinner. So “is therefore Christ the minister of sin?” means: did Christ teach us to break the law? No. Christ taught us to keep the law. This verse is a perfect scripture to combat anyone who says we are not justified by the law: by saying you are not justified by the law, you are saying Christ teaches us to sin.

precepts.point: Proverbs 24:16 also applies: a just man falls seven times and rises up again.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Paul answers the same question the same way in Romans: “What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?” God forbid.

You cannot take advantage of grace and continue breaking the law. Seeking to be justified by Christ does not make Christ the minister of sin; grace is not a license to keep transgressing the law.

precepts.point: Proverbs 24:16 also applies: a just man falls seven times and rises up again.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.”

We who seek to be justified by Christ are still found sinners, but that does not make Christ the minister of sin. The just man falls and rises up again; he does not continue in sin, he gets up and keeps the law.

precepts.point: Through the law of animal sacrifice, Paul is now dead to the law of animal sacrifice, that he might live unto God. Romans 7:4 confirms: 'ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ.' We are dead to the law of animal sacrifice by the body of Christ because Christ laid down his life for us.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
Through the law of animal sacrifice, Paul is now dead to the law of animal sacrifice, that he might live unto God. Romans confirms: “Wherefore, my brethren, ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ; that ye should be married to another, even to him who is raised from the dead, that we should bring forth fruit unto God.”

We are dead to the law of animal sacrifice by the body of Christ, because Christ laid down his life for us. Being dead to that law, we are married to him who is raised from the dead and bring forth fruit unto God.

Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: James, Cephas, and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision. The heathen: talking about the northern kingdom.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. Before certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision. Paul said: you already learned this, Peter; God showed you that you cannot call any man common or unclean. You sat with them; you convinced many of the Jews that these men were all right. But now you are wavering.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation. The class looked up dissimulation: deception, hypocrisy, pretense, deceit; in other words, being fake.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews? Peter knew better. He was corrected in front of them all, and he would have been embarrassed and ashamed. But he repented; and as a teacher, what do you teach after that? What you repented from: do not be fake.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: By the works of the law shall no flesh be justified: the verse the Christians run to, and the class will show which law Paul means.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

points: Fourteen years after, Paul went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus and communicated the gospel he preached among the Gentiles, privately to them of reputation, to those he could trust, lest he had run in vain. Titus, being a Greek, was not compelled to be circumcised; the Greek part is unfolded later.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: False brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage. Keep liberty and bondage in mind. To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour: to hell with them, whatever reputation, school, or camp they had. God accepteth no man's person, and they added nothing to me.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: They saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter, for he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles. Christ worked in Peter toward the Jews born and raised in the law and circumcised the eighth day, and the same Christ worked in Paul toward the dispersed. James, Cephas, and John gave the right hands of fellowship that we should go unto the heathen and they unto the circumcision, remembering the poor.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: When Peter was come to Antioch, in Turkey like Galatia, I withstood him to the face. He ate with the Gentiles, but when certain came from James he withdrew, fearing them of the circumcision, and the other Jews and even Barnabas dissembled with him. If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of the Gentiles, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews? You cannot teach the scattered sinners of the Gentiles who they are and then act like you are not with them; that is a bad example.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ. Here is where the other gospel and the error of the wicked come in: all you have to do is believe, you can lie, cheat, steal, and rape in the name of Jesus, as a Dominican in the Bronx once told me. Works of the law, law singular, shout out to Captain Zakar: the law of sacrifice from Nehemiah 10:33. A man no longer receives atonement by sacrificial law, for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified. Christians will run to Galatians 2:16, 3:2, and 3:5; these are their go-tos, and I am giving you the tools.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: This is Paul's second visit to Jerusalem, 14 years after his first trip (which was 3 years after his conversion on the road to Damascus). Paul went up by revelation, meaning the spirit of the Lord led him to Jerusalem.

This meant getting circumcised to reestablish the covenant with Abraham and giving an animal sacrifice to reestablish the covenant of Moses. Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them over this, so they were sent to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Acts 15:3 says they passed through Phenice and Samaria declaring the conversion of the Gentiles. Acts 15:4 shows when they came to Jerusalem, they were received by the church, apostles, and elders, and declared all things God had done with them. 'Privately to them which were of reputation' refers to the apostles and elders. 'Lest by any means I should run or had run in vain' means Paul had to check with the leadership to confirm he was on the right path.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Titus being a Greek means he was brought up in Greek customs and fashion, just like Timothy whose father was a Greek. He was not a Caucasian.
Yet even Titus, who had a book written after him, fell away through these doctrines about circumcision and animal sacrifice. If Titus could fall, anybody could fall.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: He was an Israelite raised in Greek ways. 'Was compelled to be circumcised' shows the Pharisees were going around forcefully telling people they had to be circumcised and return to animal sacrifice. The false brethren brought in unawares are identified in Acts 15:5: 'there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying that it was needful to circumcise them and to command them to keep the law of Moses.' These were believers who infiltrated the congregation with this doctrine.

John 4:20-22 records the Samaritan woman saying 'Our fathers worshipped in this mountain,' referring to the northern kingdom's worship of false gods, and Christ replied 'Ye worship ye know not what.. salvation is of the Jews.' Deuteronomy 12:5-7 commands all tribes to bring burnt offerings and sacrifices to the place the Lord chose, which was Jerusalem. So if animal sacrifice were still in effect, the northern kingdom could never be grafted back in because they broke the covenants of promise.

Animal sacrifice could not make a person perfect because there were certain sins (homosexuality, adultery, murder, witchcraft) for which you were put to death with no atonement. Under Christ, we receive mercy and the opportunity to overcome sin.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Paul says the disciples did not give place to the heretics, not even for one hour. As soon as they heard the heresy, they said you have to go.

Paul reads Psalms 51 every day, praying to endure and not become a castaway. The disciples did not give time for heretics to spread their doctrine because they understood there are weak-minded people in the body that are easily deceived.
Any heretical doctrine brought into the congregation is dealt with immediately. You come with any type of doctrines into the congregation, you will be removed.
The disciples did not debate heretics. They did not argue with them.
This is how the truth of the gospel continues with the people.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Paul says these people pushing false doctrine seemed to be somebody, puffed up, of nobility and specialty. But Paul said it made no matter to him.
They took some people from the congregation and felt good about themselves, but it did not harm the apostles. God accepted no man's person, meaning God does not care about these people who left.
He would use you then cast you away. They who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to Paul.
They did not do the apostles any harm. They did themselves harm.
They were not fighting against the disciples but fighting against God. The class ends with Paul noting they covered verses 1 through 6, and next week they will continue from verse 7 through 21.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: In Acts 11:2-3, those of the circumcision contended with Peter for going to men uncircumcised. Romans 3:1 shows the Jews were called the circumcision because they kept the covenant of circumcision established to Abraham.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Paul's ministry was given to him by Christ and was directed to the uncircumcision, just as Peter's ministry was to the circumcision, also wrought by Christ. The uncircumcision was also called the Gentiles; these terms mean one and the same.
In Acts 11:1, the apostles heard that the Gentiles had received the word of God, referring specifically to Cornelius. In Acts 10:31-36, Peter explains his encounter with Cornelius.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: When Paul came to Jerusalem, the apostles perceived the Most High was dealing with him based on his ministry and the people he was waking up. You can tell the spirit on someone by how they move.

If the spirit of the Most High is in you, it compels you to keep pushing forward in the truth no matter how tired or exhausted. Those who are faking it can only do it for so long before they pull back, become less visible, and eventually leave.
Verse 9 introduces a third term: the heathen. Paul was sent to the heathen, same people called uncircumcision and Gentiles.

Ezekiel 20:31-32 shows God rebukes Israel for idolatry and says Israel declared 'we will be as the heathen' by following other nations' customs. When Israelites go outside their laws and follow other nations, they are called heathens.

Ezekiel 25:8 shows even other nations recognized when Israel became like the heathen. 2 Esdras 2:33-34 records Ezra calling Israel 'ye heathen' because they set the commandments of God at naught. Acts 15:22-23 confirms this: the apostles sent letters to 'the brethren which are of the Gentiles' in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
They are called brethren of the Gentiles. Romans 9:3-4 proves the apostles' brethren are Israelites.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Acts 15:22 shows this encounter that Paul is explaining to the Galatians. The apostles and elders sent chosen men (Judas surnamed Barsabas and Silas, chief men among the brethren) with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch.
They were given a charge to go to the brethren of the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: This history is not recorded in Acts. After Paul was in Antioch doing his ministry, Peter came along later.
Paul confronted Peter to his face because he was at fault. Peter, being the head apostle and second in command from Christ, still made mistakes.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Before certain men came from James, Peter ate with the Gentiles (Israelites living in a Gentile way of life). But when the southern kingdom arrived, Peter withdrew and separated himself from the northern kingdom out of respect of persons.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: He did not want to be seen eating with them. The other Jews also dissembled with him, and even Barnabas was carried away, withdrawing himself from the northern kingdom, not sitting or eating with them.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Paul confronted Peter in front of everybody. He said: you claim to be a Jew, salvation is of the Jews, and you are supposed to be an example, but you are doing the same thing the northern kingdom was doing.
You are following their footsteps rather than being an example. You are showing respect of persons and living like them while trying to teach them to follow after the Jews.
You are being a hypocrite in your actions. Paul did not let things slide.
He had no respect of persons and did not fear any man regardless of their status.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Being Jews by nature means being born as a Jew and keeping the laws by nature. They are not like the Gentiles being sinners (breaking the law).

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: This is a very famous scripture used by Christians to argue against keeping the law. But Paul is making reference to a specific law.

Romans 2:13 says 'the doers of the law shall be justified,' which refers to the commandments (as shown by Romans 2:17-22 listing do not steal, do not commit adultery, abhor idols). So we ARE justified by keeping the commandments.

But in Galatians 2:16, 'the works of the law' refers to a different law. Acts 13:38-39 clarifies: through Christ is preached forgiveness of sins, and all that believe are justified from all things from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.

Under the law of Moses (animal sacrifice), you could not be justified for certain sins like homosexuality, adultery, witchcraft: you were put to death. Hebrews 10:4-8 proves it: it is not possible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.
Animal sacrifice was temporary. When Christ came, sacrifice and offerings were no longer in effect because Christ would be the ultimate sacrifice.
We were not justified by the sacrificial law, but by Christ. Sirach 42:15 confirms that the works of the Lord are His law, statutes, and commandments.

Exodus 18:20 says 'show them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do,' meaning the ordinances and the laws. Isaiah 45:25 prophesied that in the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified.
Habakkuk 2:4 says the just shall live by his faith, meaning the justified seed of Israel shall live by faith in Christ rather than by animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Even when seeking to be justified by Christ, we are still found sinners because sin is the transgression of the law (1 John 3:4). Even under Christ, if you break the law, you are a sinner. 'Is therefore Christ the minister of sin?' means: did Christ teach us to break the law?
No. Christ taught us to keep the law.
Romans 6:1 says shall we continue in sin that grace may abound? God forbid.

You cannot take advantage of grace and continue breaking the law. This verse is a perfect scripture to combat anyone who says we are not justified by the law: by saying you are not justified by the law, you are saying Christ teaches us to sin.
Proverbs 24:16 also applies: a just man falls seven times and rises up again.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: If you used to be a fornicator or adulterer and you overcame those sins but then go back into them, you are building again the things you destroyed. You made provision for the flesh and went back into old sins.
You become a transgressor just like you were from the beginning. All the work you did in overcoming sin was for naught.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Through the law of animal sacrifice, Paul is now dead to the law of animal sacrifice, that he might live unto God. Romans 7:4 confirms: 'ye also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ.' We are dead to the law of animal sacrifice by the body of Christ because Christ laid down his life for us.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: The old man is crucified with Christ. Even though Paul lives in the flesh, Christ lives in him.

Christ gave him the opportunity and chance to repent and receive forgiveness of sins. Living by faith in Christ means living under His grace and mercies, believing that Christ died for our sins, rather than believing in the law of animal sacrifice.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Paul says he will not frustrate the grace of God, meaning he will not prevent God's grace from coming to fruition by pushing animal sacrifice or going against Christ. If righteousness comes by the law of animal sacrifice, then Christ the Messiah died in vain.
All the prophecies pertaining to Christ coming and dying for our sins would be for nothing if we continue in the law of animal sacrifice.
